cohort: 627 twin pregnancies with delivery from January 2016 to December 2019
finding: Cesarean section was associated with higher rates of preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, but lower rates of PPROM, postpartum bleeding, and neonatal morbidity compared to vaginal delivery in twin pregnancies.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a lower incidence of PPROM and postpartum bleeding, as well as higher neonatal weights and 5-minute Apgar scores compared to vaginal delivery in twin pregnancies.
